claims.text: At stage-3 ProductListScreen shows a StatusBanner with StatusTone.warning above the saved list when it is out of date; QueuedOrdersScreen shows a StatusBanner per queued order.
At stage-3 lib/design/components/ holds exactly three widgets: LoadingView, MessageView and StatusBanner.
LoadingView is a centered CircularProgressIndicator; MessageView is one centered message with at most one action; StatusBanner is a message colored by its tone with at most one action.
StatusTone is an enum with four values: info, success, warning, error.

At stage-3 ProductListScreen, ProductDetailScreen, OrderDetailScreen and CreateOrderScreen use LoadingView while loading and MessageView on a load error; ProductListScreen and QueuedOrdersScreen also use MessageView for an empty list.
StatusBanner's constructor takes required message and tone and optional actionLabel and onAction; it has no Color parameter.

StatusBanner._colors maps info to secondaryContainer/onSecondaryContainer and error to errorContainer/onErrorContainer from ColorScheme, success and warning to StatusColors' success/onSuccess and warning/onWarning.

StatusBanner.build draws a Material with the tone's background, padding Insets.tile, the message in textTheme.bodyMedium with the text color, and the action as a TextButton with that foreground color, only when actionLabel is not null.
At stage-3 no file under DonHang.App/lib/screens contains the text 'color' in any case; screens pass StatusBanner a tone, never a color.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: git grep -i color -- DonHang.App/lib/screens (no match)

claims.text: CreateOrderScreen at stage-3 shows the server error as StatusBanner(tone: StatusTone.error) and disables the submit button (onPressed null) while _sending.
In QueuedOrdersScreen._entry a waiting order is info, a rejected one error with a remove action, a sent one success, or warning when priceChanged; sent banners have an open-order action.
In Dart, adding an optional named parameter to a constructor leaves existing calls compiling; renaming or removing a named parameter makes every call that passes it a compile error.
claims.source_hint: Dart language tour: Functions > Named parameters; Dart compile errors for undefined named parameter

claims.text: A component's parameter should be added only when a screen needs it, when the component has several callers, because each parameter becomes part of the contract they depend on.

status_banner_test.dart runs one testWidgets per StatusTone.values under buildTheme(donHangBrand, Brightness.light), checks the text, taps the 'Undo' TextButton, checks the callback ran and compares the Material's color with expectedBackground.
status_banner_test.dart has a second test: a StatusBanner without actionLabel shows no TextButton.
When screens may pass colors, banners of the same meaning tend to drift apart; a tone keeps the look decided in one place. A meaning the four tones lack calls for a new tone, not a color parameter.
A folder inside the app is enough for a component library when one app uses it; a separate package pays off when several apps share the components.

At stage-3 the doc comments of LoadingView, MessageView and StatusBanner each say where the component does not fit; LoadingView's says it is "not for a button that is busy: disable the button instead".
AuthCallbackScreen at stage-3 builds its own CircularProgressIndicator with a signingIn text below it; LoadingView takes no parameters besides key.

At stage-3 `grep -rn -F "StatusBanner(" DonHang.App/lib/screens` prints 8 lines: 6 in queued_orders_screen.dart (3 in _entry, one call covering both sent cases; 3 in _syncMessage), 1 in product_list_screen.dart, 1 in create_order_screen.dart.
Screens write const LoadingView(); const constructors let Flutter short-circuit most of the rebuild work for that widget when its parent rebuilds.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: lib/screens/*_screen.dart 'const LoadingView()'; Flutter docs: performance best practices, const constructors

claims.text: git switch --detach <tag> checks out the commit a tag points to without creating a branch.

A separate Dart package is its own project that an app adds as a dependency; a split made too early shows when every change to StatusBanner also means changing the one app that uses it, across a boundary nobody else needs.
claims.source_hint: Dart docs: Using packages (dependencies in pubspec.yaml)

claims.text: Material is the Flutter widget that paints a colored surface; its color property is the surface's background.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API: material library, Material class, color property
